summary: Weed Lookout is a 1926 Aermotor LX-24 tower on the Lincoln National Forest, the oldest standing lookout there, still standing and NRHP-listed since 1988.

facts.design: Aermotor LX-24, 48-foot steel tower with a 7x7-foot steel cab

access.note: On USDA Forest Service land (Sacramento Ranger District, Lincoln National Forest); no rental or stay program found in sources reviewed.

visit.trail_note: Specific trail access not confirmed in sources reviewed; check Lincoln National Forest Sacramento Ranger District guidance.

events.note: Aermotor LX-24 tower erected on Sacramento Ranger District, Lincoln National Forest; oldest standing lookout on the forest.
Original wooden stairs replaced with metal steps.
Cabin and shed at the site were removed.
Added to the National Register of Historic Places, January 28, 1988, as part of the National Forest Fire Lookouts in the Southwestern Region multiple-property listing.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, August 30, 2015 (per queue brief, drawn from NHLR detail page).

evidence.supports: Built 1926, Aermotor LX-24, 48 feet, 7x7 cab, oldest standing on the forest
evidence.quote: This Aermotor LX-24 lookout is located on the Sacramento Ranger District, Lincoln National Forest, and was erected in 1926. The Weed lookout is the oldest standing lookout on the Lincoln National Forest. The tower is 48 feet high and is topped by a 7X7 foot steel cab.
The site did contain a cabin and shed, which were removed in 1978. The tower originally had wooden steps but were replaced by metal ones in 1966.
The Weed Lookout Tower, in Lincoln National Forest in Otero County, New Mexico near Sacramento, New Mexico, was built in 1926. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1988.

evidence.supports: Alamo Lookout as a comparable nearby 1926 Aermotor structure
evidence.quote: Like the Weed Lookout, the Alamo Lookout was erected in 1926 and had a wood framed Observer's cabin
